b: There are now more social media platforms than any one person can reasonably keep up with — and yet somehow the advice is always 'you should be on all of them.' (Don't worry, we're not going to tell you that!)
Whether you're building your personal brand or managing social media marketing for a business, the challenge is figuring out which platforms are worth your time.

This guide compares 24 social media platforms in 2026, covering their audience sizes, popular content formats, and what they're best suited for. From familiar giants like Facebook and Instagram to rising players like Threads and Bluesky, you'll find information to help you decide which platforms deserve a place in your social media strategy.

And remember: you don't need to be on every social media site to grow. Start with two or three platforms that fit your audience, the content you enjoy creating, and the time you have available. If you're wondering what to post, our analysis explores which content formats perform best across different platforms.
The biggest platforms still have billions of users: Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, and YouTube offer enormous audiences, but that doesn't mean they're right for every brand.
Video offers plenty of options: From YouTube tutorials to TikTok videos and Instagram Reels, there's more than one way to reach people through video.
Looking beyond X? Threads and Bluesky offer different ways to join public conversations and connect with interest-based communities.
You don't need to be everywhere: Start with two or three platforms that fit your audience and the content you can consistently create.
Overview of the most popular social media platforms

Top 24 social media apps and platforms for 2026
We've ranked this list by monthly active users (MAUs) — basically, how many people use the platform each month.
A platform with billions of users sounds impressive, but if your audience isn't there, it won't matter how big it is.
Start by figuring out where your audience spends time online, then focus your efforts on the platforms where you're most likely to reach and engage them.
Facebook remains the largest social media platform in the world, with more than 3 billion monthly active users — over one-third of the global population.

It continues to be a popular choice for social media marketing, thanks to its broad audience reach and support for nearly every type of content format. It’s also a strong option for advertisers, with a huge range of targeting options that help you reach the right people.
Works well for text, images, video content, stories, and live streams
Features like Facebook Groups and Facebook Messenger allow deeper community building and customer engagement
Facebook Ads Manager offers audience targeting options for paid social media campaigns
Pro tip: Here’s how to grow your Facebook following and make the most of the algorithm by creating content your audience wants to engage with.
Best time to post on Facebook: We analyzed millions of posts to help you find the best times for engagement.
Instagram is one of the most visual social media platforms, built for sharing photos, videos, Stories, and short-form video content like Reels.
With around 3 billion monthly active users, it’s especially popular with Gen Z and millennials.
A wide range of formats, including reels, stories, and live video
Discovery features like the Explore tab, reel recommendations, and hashtags
Encourages user-generated content through mentions, tags, and branded campaigns

You can switch to an Instagram business profile to access in-depth analytics and business tools. It’s also easy to crosspost to Facebook and Threads since they’re all part of the Meta family of platforms.
Best time to post on Instagram: Based on millions of posts, we found the times most likely to drive engagement.
WhatsApp is the world’s most popular messaging app, used in over 180 countries by around 3 billion people every month.
It started as a way to message friends, but plenty of businesses now use it for customer support, updates, and marketing.
The WhatsApp Business app helps small businesses share updates, show off their products, and answer customer questions directly
Larger teams can use the WhatsApp Business Platform to automate responses and integrate customer communication with other business tools
Sharing limited-time deals with customers who've opted in
Reaching audiences in markets where WhatsApp is widely used, like Brazil, India, and Indonesia

WhatsApp's end-to-end encrypted personal messaging makes it a popular choice for direct communication with customers. And with features like channels and status, businesses have more ways to share updates and reach new audiences.
With viewers watching over a billion hours of YouTube content on TVs every day, YouTube remains a popular platform for brands investing in video content.
And here's something interesting: YouTube even accounts for a significant share of all U.S. television viewing, competing with streaming services like Netflix, Disney+, and Amazon Prime Video.
Why YouTube matters for your marketing strategy:
Supports both long-form and short-form videos (including YouTube Shorts)
Great for evergreen content, tutorials, behind-the-scenes videos, and storytelling
YouTube is also a search engine, which means the right keywords, thumbnails, and titles can help your videos get discovered long after you post them
Whether you’re new to YouTube or refining your current presence, here’s how to grow on YouTube and start building a community through content.
Learn more about the YouTube algorithm and how to grow your audience.
Best time to post on YouTube: We analyzed millions of videos to find the best publishing times.
TikTok is one of the largest short-form video content platforms, especially among younger audiences.
With 2 billion monthly active users globally, it's a popular choice for creators, small businesses, and brands looking to show up in a more personal, creative way.
Users can create videos up to 10 minutes long (and up to 60 minutes when uploaded from a device) with built-in music, voice effects, and editing tools
The algorithm pays close attention to what people watch and engage with — which means even smaller accounts can reach new audiences if the content resonates.
Challenges, duets, and trends give brands opportunities to join conversations and create content with their communities
If your target demographic includes Gen Z or younger millennials, TikTok can be a powerful place to connect through authentic, fast-moving content.
Want to grow? Learn how the TikTok algorithm works and how to get more followers — from content hooks to posting strategy.

Pro tip: You don't need to post multiple times a day to grow on TikTok. Buffer's analysis of 11.4 million TikTok posts found that increasing your posting frequency from once a week to two to five times a week offered the biggest lift in views relative to the extra posts.
Best time to post on TikTok: Our research breaks down the best posting windows for reach and engagement.
Interested in expanding your social media presence internationally? WeChat could be your gateway to one of the largest online markets in the world.

Developed by Chinese tech giant Tencent, WeChat is one of the most versatile social media platforms. Originally a messaging app, it has grown into an all-in-one platform where users can send messages, make payments, shop online, book rides, and more.
Offers branded WeChat Official Accounts for businesses to share content and engage with followers
Enables businesses to run ads, build mini programs (apps within WeChat), and reach audiences through WeChat Moments
Supports shopping and payments within the app, with Weixin mini programs facilitating trillions of RMB in transactions
If you're trying to reach users in China — where platforms like Facebook, Instagram, and X (formerly Twitter) are restricted — you’ll want to be on WeChat.
You can also partner with Chinese influencers to promote your brand through articles, videos, and other content within the WeChat ecosystem.
Telegram is a popular messaging app known for its privacy-first approach and flexibility.
While it started as a simple chat tool, it's grown into a social media platform with channels, communities, bots, and broadcast tools.
End-to-end encryption for secret chats, although regular chats aren't end-to-end encrypted by default
Groups of up to 200,000 members and channels with unlimited subscribers
Bots and automation for delivering content, collecting feedback, and supporting customer interactions
Channels let you share updates directly with subscribers, which makes Telegram really handy for newsletters, product announcements, and community building.

While Telegram doesn't offer the same content discovery experience as TikTok or Instagram, features like recommended channels help users find new communities. You can also use bots and mini apps to offer interactive experiences, which can be useful for tech-savvy brands and creators.

Snapchat pioneered the idea of disappearing content and vertical video — both of which have become staples across other social media platforms like Instagram and TikTok. With over 970 million monthly active users globally, Snapchat remains a powerful messaging app and visual content platform, especially among younger audiences.
Why Snapchat should have a place in your strategy:
Strong engagement with Gen Z and U.S. teens (over half of them use the app)
Features like lenses, Bitmoji, and private stories make it highly interactive, with hundreds of millions of users engaging with AR daily
Tools like Spotlight help creators reach audiences through short-form videos, while My AI offers an in-app chatbot experience

While Snapchat may not be as central to your social media marketing strategy as Instagram or TikTok, it still plays a key role in reaching specific target demographics, especially if your brand skews younger or lifestyle-driven.

Douyin is the Chinese sister app of TikTok, developed by ByteDance and launched before its global counterpart — which is why the interface might feel familiar. The two share a core codebase, but operate on completely separate networks.
With over 850 million monthly active users, Douyin is one of China's leading social media platforms and a powerhouse in short-form video content and social commerce.
In-app shopping features allow users to buy products through videos, livestreams, and dedicated storefronts
Personalized recommendations help users discover videos, creators, and products based on their interests
Popular for tutorials, product reviews, behind-the-scenes content, and shopping hauls
For brands and creators looking to reach audiences in China, Douyin is worth exploring for its video content, livestreams, and in-app shopping features.

International brands may need to meet additional requirements to sell on Douyin or work with local partners to manage their presence. Here's what overseas businesses should know about opening a Douyin store.
Kuaishou is one of China’s largest video-focused social media platforms, and a key competitor to TikTok (known as Douyin in China).
With around 800 million monthly active users, it's known for its community-focused approach and popularity beyond China's biggest cities, including lower-tier cities and rural regions.
Strong emphasis on everyday storytelling and creator-audience relationships
Supports long-form videos, short-form content, and livestreaming
Built-in e-commerce features let users discover and purchase products through videos, livestreams, and storefronts

Kuaishou has a reputation for community engagement and relationships between creators and their followers. That community focus makes Kuaishou a good fit if you’re targeting the Chinese market and interested in social commerce.

Reddit is a hybrid discussion platform and social network made up of thousands of niche communities called subreddits. It’s a go-to platform for in-depth conversations, advice, crowd-sourced knowledge, and cultural commentary.
Communities exist for virtually every topic — from skincare to startups to AI
Many users participate under pseudonyms, making it easier to discuss topics without using their real names
Subreddits like r/beauty and r/entrepreneur offer insights into the questions, experiences, and recommendations people share with one another

Reddit gives brands and creators a direct look at what people are asking, discussing, and recommending. Participating in relevant communities can help you understand your audience and build relationships over time.

Many subreddits have strict rules around self-promotion, so check each community's guidelines before posting. Focus on offering helpful advice, asking thoughtful questions, and sharing relevant resources when they're welcome.
Learn how to find content ideas from Reddit trends.
Pinterest is where inspiration meets action. It’s a visual social media platform that functions more like a discovery engine than a traditional feed.
Users “pin” images and videos linked to blogs, products, and landing pages — making Pinterest a useful channel for driving website traffic and product discovery.
According to Pinterest's own research, users are 7x more likely to purchase a product they've previously saved
Especially popular for niches like fashion, home decor, wellness, DIY, and food
More than half of Pinterest's users are Gen Z, making it a useful platform for reaching younger audiences
Searchable, evergreen content can continue attracting visitors long after it's published
And while Pinterest is known for images, video is worth experimenting with. Buffer's research found that video Pins earned 83% higher median engagement than image Pins.
Whether you're promoting blog content, e-commerce listings, or tutorials, Pinterest helps you show up when people are actively searching for ideas.
Just getting started? Here’s how to use Pinterest for business and grow your following from zero.
Weibo is a Chinese microblogging platform that combines features of X (formerly Twitter) and Instagram.
With about 560 million monthly active users, Weibo is one of China’s biggest social networks. It’s where trends take off, and influencers do a lot of their brand work.
Why Weibo is a top choice:
Content includes images, videos, stories, live streams, and hashtags
Popular for conversations about entertainment, news, beauty, fashion, and technology
Offers verified business accounts, advertising options, and opportunities to collaborate with influencers

Compared to WeChat's emphasis on messaging and private interactions, Weibo’s audience is younger and more trend-focused. It's a place where trends and public conversations unfold and where brands can join cultural conversations in real time.
X, formerly known as Twitter, continues to be a major social media platform, known for real-time conversations, trending topics, and short-form updates.
While the platform has undergone significant changes since its rebrand in 2023, it remains a place for brands, creators, and communities to discuss news and events as they unfold.
Emphasis on timely content — from breaking news to live commentary
A home for text-first content, making it ideal for thought leadership, humor, and hot takes
Public conversations give brands an opportunity to respond to customer questions and feedback
X has changed a lot, and it’s become quite a divisive place for some groups. But if you post fast and your niche still hangs out there, it’s worth keeping.
Best time to post on X: Our analysis of millions of posts shows when engagement is highest.
QQ, also developed by Tencent, was once China’s leading instant messaging app before WeChat took the lead.
Today, with over 520 million monthly active users, QQ still holds strong, especially among younger users, gamers, and professionals looking for lightweight communication and file sharing.
Why QQ has a loyal user base:
Supports desktop messaging, group chats, and file sharing (over 25 MB)
Offers a social feed, avatar customization, and built-in online games
Doesn’t require a phone number to sign up — appealing to students and users without smartphones

QQ also has communities built around shared interests like gaming, anime, and entertainment. If younger Chinese audiences are your target, being active in these spaces is a good way to learn what they’re into and how they talk about it..
QQ isn’t a major channel for global marketing, but it’s definitely worth knowing about if you’re trying to understand China’s social landscape.

Threads, developed by Meta as a companion to Instagram, launched in mid-2023. It quickly became one of the fastest-growing social media apps in history and reached 100 million sign-ups in just a few days.
A text-first platform for short-form updates, commentary, and casual conversation
Integrated with Instagram, making it easier to set up your profile and connect with people you already know
An alternative to X, with topic tags that help people discover conversations around shared interests and can increase post visibility
Threads gives creators, founders, and brands a place to build connections through conversational content. Many use it for behind-the-scenes updates, audience questions, and informal thoughts.

Pro tip: Replying to comments is worth making time for, too. In Buffer's analysis of 128,000+ Threads posts, posts where creators replied to comments saw 42% higher engagement than their usual baseline.
Best time to post on Threads: Our analysis of millions of posts shows when engagement is highest.

LinkedIn is the leading professional networking platform, originally built for job seekers and recruiters, but now just as valuable for creators, small business owners, and brands. It's become a hub for sharing ideas, building authority, and growing your personal brand.
Why LinkedIn is a must for professionals and brands:
Ideal for B2B marketing, industry insights, and employer branding
Powerful space to establish thought leadership through articles, newsletters, document posts, and videos
Offers ways to connect with industry peers, potential customers, and decision-makers through posts and discussions

LinkedIn is also seeing more activity around professional conversations since knowledge-focused posts and time spent reading comments are both increasing. For brands and creators, that's another reason to focus on sharing expertise and participating in relevant discussions.

P.S. If you're deciding what to post, Buffer's analysis of social media content formats found that LinkedIn carousels earned a median engagement rate of 21.77%, outperforming videos, images, and text posts in the dataset.
Learn how the LinkedIn algorithm works and how to grow your followers.
Best time to post on LinkedIn: Our data shows the top times for engagement and visibility based on millions of posts.
Quora is a discussion platform built around questions and answers where users share knowledge, give advice, and rank responses through upvotes and views.
With 400 million monthly unique visitors, Quora continues to be a valuable space for brands and creators to share their expertise and reach people researching topics relevant to their business.
People use Quora to research products, explore topics, and find answers to specific questions
Helpful answers can appear in Google search results and continue attracting readers over time
A space to showcase subject-matter expertise and share relevant resources when they genuinely help answer a question
Offers advertising options for B2B brands, including account-based targeting

On Quora, your audience is already asking the questions — you just have to answer them. You can contribute to industry-relevant discussions, create a Quora Business Profile, or run ads through Quora's advertising platform.

Pro tip: Encourage founders or subject-matter experts on your team to answer questions in their areas of expertise. Their firsthand experience can make answers more useful and credible. If they mention your product or company, they should disclose their affiliation.
Xiaohongshu, also known as RedNote or Little Red Book, is a Chinese social media platform that blends lifestyle content, product discovery, and e-commerce.
It’s often described as a hybrid of Instagram, Pinterest, and Amazon reviews that’s especially popular among Gen Z and millennial women.
Why RedNote is a rising star:
Combines user-generated content with product recommendations, tutorials, and reviews
Functions as a discovery and search platform, with most users using its search feature
Offers in-app shopping features, including storefronts and livestream shopping
Especially influential in beauty, fashion, wellness, travel, and luxury niches

RedNote has also attracted international attention, particularly when creators explored alternatives to TikTok in early 2025. For brands, the big draw is that people use it like a search engine for product recommendations.
If you’re targeting the Chinese market or exploring social commerce trends, RedNote is a platform to watch closely.
Discord started as a communication platform for gamers, but today, it powers communities across everything from entrepreneurship and crypto to education and creator spaces.
